questions.prompt: A team wants to measure resources outside its allowed regions before blocking deployments. Which policy effect reports violations without rejecting requests?

options.explanation: It records noncompliance without acting as Deny.
It can reject noncompliant create/update requests.
It changes supported properties rather than only observing.
It can deploy related configuration and is not purely reporting.

questions.prompt: A Modify policy assignment adds a supported costCenter tag to new resources. Existing untagged resources appear as noncompliant after evaluation but remain unchanged. The assignment has a managed identity with the roles required by the definition. Without redeploying the workloads or changing the policy rule, which action applies the tag to these existing resources?

options.text: Create a remediation task for the existing noncompliant resources.
options.explanation: Modify evaluation marks existing resources noncompliant; a remediation task applies the correction using the authorized assignment identity.

options.text: Trigger another compliance evaluation for the same assignment.
options.explanation: Another evaluation discovers noncompliance but does not modify existing resources.

options.text: Grant additional resource permissions to the administrator who created the assignment.
options.explanation: The authorized assignment identity performs remediation. Extra permissions for the administrator do not start correction.

options.text: Change the assignment to an Audit effect and run another evaluation.
options.explanation: Audit reports violations rather than adding the missing tag.

questions.prompt: A DeployIfNotExists policy deployed a diagnostic setting that sends resource logs to an existing Log Analytics workspace. An administrator removes the policy assignment. No cleanup automation runs and neither the diagnostic setting nor the workspace is deleted or changed. What is the diagnostic setting's state after assignment removal?

options.text: It remains configured to send logs to the workspace.
options.explanation: The assignment and deployed diagnostic setting are separate resources. Removing the assignment does not undo the diagnostic configuration.

options.text: It is deleted when the assignment is deleted.
options.explanation: Deleting the assignment does not itself delete the separately deployed diagnostic setting.

options.text: It remains present but its log categories are automatically disabled.
options.explanation: No operation changes the diagnostic setting. Assignment removal does not edit its enabled categories.

options.text: It remains present but its workspace destination is automatically cleared.
options.explanation: The workspace destination is part of the diagnostic configuration, which the scenario leaves unchanged.
